why: The inserted special-case penalised cuts that leave the left fragment ending on a finite/reporting verb, so the scorer shifted cuts away from verb-final prefixes (e.g. merged 'Schlafen ‖ Sie' into 'Schlafen Sie ...' and kept verb+object together). That change helped the smallest-piece bin (≤3 pieces: +0.0092) but displaced cuts into other boundaries—sometimes splitting named entities and enumerations (e.g. 'Mission Bay' was split)—producing net small harms in the mid/longer bins (≤5: −0.0161, ≤10: −0.0054) and nearly balanced n_worse/n_better.
lesson: A later revision should respect that penalising predicate-ending prefixes helps very short-piece cuts but can push cuts into names/enumerations and hurt mid-length cases, so its scope must be constrained to avoid creating those splits.
